messages:
dmitri: saw p99 spike and throughput drop ~30% on prod-gpu-pool starting 09:12 UTC, affects mostly medium-seq traffic (seq ~512).

alice: confirmed on traces - many requests picked a new 'flash_select_v2' kernel after today's driver/infra roll. p50 ok, p95 -> small increase, p99 huge. :eyes:

ben: stack from profiler (short):
```
Kernel timeline sample:
flash_select_v2/launch   42.3 ms
flash_attn_v1/launch    11.2 ms
triton_gemm_fallback    7.8 ms
kv_cache_touch          0.7 ms
kv_cache_evict         13.6 ms  <-- spikes correlate with p99
memcpy H2D              1.1 ms
```

lina: curious, we only changed triton runtime minor bump and CUDA driver update this morning. infra-bot says a canary rolled triton 2.3 and CUDA 535.xx at 08:50. ops-bot: "deploy triton/2.3.0 -> prod-gpu-pool"

dmitri: hypothesis: selector heuristics in flash_select_v2 prefer a different tiling/workspace for medium seq, which causes more temporary workspace allocations leading to kv cache eviction pressure (and thrashing).

alice: repro steps I used on a canary small cluster: run mixed batch sizes with warm KV cache, then push steady medium-seq QPS. p99 rises after ~120s when cache eviction rate climbs.

ben: quick mitigation? Can we pin kernel selector to old behavior via env flag? I see a flag `AUTO_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=legacy` in runtime.

lina: tried setting `AUTO_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=legacy` on a single node, p99 returned to baseline in ~30s. Good signal.

dmitri: ok canary rollback plan: set env on all app nodes to `AUTO_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=legacy` and throttle the triton rollout. ops-bot: submitting rollback patch now.

alice: also collected nvprof summary for one sample request (before/after):
```
Before: flash_attn_v1 9.7ms, kv_hits 99%, p99 68ms
After:  flash_select_v2 41.2ms, kv_hits 84%, kv_evictions++ -> p99 420ms
```

ben: adding a short-term scheduler fix: reduce max workspace for the new kernel so it falls back earlier instead of allocating huge workspace. Will put a canary config in sandbox.

dmitri: long-term: need to add a kernel selection unit test that exercises mixed-batch medium-seq traffic and asserts no regression in kv_eviction_rate. File a follow-up in eng-runtime board.

lina: tickets: ENGRT-3742 (rollback + canary), ENGRT-3743 (selector unit test), ENGRT-3744 (prof trace exporter for kv eviction counters).

alice: heads-up to customer-success for any noisy tenants impacted; looks limited to a small subset of medium-seq workloads but good to notify.

ops-bot: rollback job started on pool prod-gpu-pool nodes: 6 -> in-progress.

dmitri: will monitor p99 and kv eviction metric `kv.evictions/s` (dash updated). If stable after rollback, revert triton bump and add gating test.

ben: follow-up: I'll push a small patch to kernel-selector to prefer smaller workspace for batch sizes < 8 for seq in [256,1024]. Testing now.

alice: thanks all. posting logs and profiler traces to the incident folder. short retro after stable. :thumbsup:
